results.title: World Humanities Report on South Asia Showcases How the Disciplines Help Address Challenges Like Inequality, Environmental Issues, and Digitalisation - Frontline
results.content: ### A new report shows how humanities disciplines shape critical thinking in universities, social movements, addressing contemporary challenges from inequality to digital activism. The World Humanities Report highlights how humanities thrive in multiple locations—universities, classrooms, social movements, and collective solidarities. “How have the humanities helped researchers, activists, thinkers, and interrogators understand the contradictions, conundrums, and possibilities of our contemporary time?” Shedding light on the diverse and crucial contributions of the humanities across South Asia, particularly in India, a new report tries to answer this question, and more. Yet, humanities-anchored reflections occur, and the report highlights this fact...this report focusses on the enabling side of the humanities and their capacity to interrogate our society and the larger world,” Bishnu N. Mohapatra, anchor of the report for India and South Asia, tells *Frontline*. N. Mohapatra, the anchor of the report for India and South Asia explains how the report “focusses on the enabling side of the humanities and their capacity to interrogate our society and the larger world”.

results.title: NFC Research and Awards » Victoria College
results.content: About Victoria / The Northrop Frye Centre / NFC Research and Awards. The NFC Undergraduate Research Award provides Vic students with the opportunity to further their involvement with Humanities and Social Sciences research. If your proposal is successful, in addition to the research funds and mentoring, you will be given the title of **Northrop Frye Centre Undergraduate Fellow** and invited to participate in NFC activities during the academic year following conferral of the award. The Northrop Frye Centre is currently accepting applications for the **2026-2027 Undergraduate Research Awards** for Victoria College students interested in research in the Humanities or Social Sciences. Northrop Frye Centre Doctoral Fellows will be expected to engage with students and the larger intellectual community at Victoria College and present a lecture or seminar related to their research. The Centre for the Study of the United States and the Northrop Frye Centre at Victoria College will be making **two awards,** valued at **$2,500** each, for undergraduate students in the 2026-2027 academic year.
